title: "we will do and we will hear"
hookLine: "we will do and we will hear" — practice before belief
last: YOU'LL LIMP AND YOU'LL BE BLESSED.

lines: AN ANSWER IN THE WRONG ORDER.
cards: Three months out of Egypt, a crowd of former slaves is camped at the foot of a mountain in the desert. They've been told to wash, to wait, to keep back from the slopes.
On the third morning there's thunder, lightning, a thick cloud on the peak, and the sound of a horn growing louder and louder until the whole camp is shaking.

Later, what this new life with God will ask is read out loud to them. And the people give an answer, all together, that the rabbis would keep coming back to. It's two words in Hebrew, and they're in the wrong order.
Today: the mountain, and the answer.

teach.h: THE MOUNTAIN WHERE TORAH IS GIVEN.
teach.b: Sinai is the mountain where, in the Torah's story, God gives the Torah to Israel. Where exactly it stood is uncertain, and the text isn't interested in the map. What matters is what happens there.
After the laws are read, the people say: "All that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey."
In Hebrew: na'aseh v'nishma. We will do, and we will hear. Look at the order.
The usual order runs the other way: explain it to me first, then I'll decide whether to do it. Here the doing comes first, and the understanding follows.

The rabbis tell a story about that moment: when Israel put doing before hearing, a voice from heaven asked, who revealed to my children this secret that the angels use? Teachers hear in it practice before belief.
You light the candles, as on day two, before you have a theory of candles. The meaning grows out of the doing. The rabbis also argued about that day, and they wrote the argument down.

One teacher said the mountain was held over the people like a barrel, as if they had no real choice. Others answered that they accepted freely, and accepted again in later generations. Both readings are kept.
And one more teaching: every Jewish soul, even of people not yet born, stood at Sinai, converts too.

teach.h: WE WILL DO, AND WE WILL HEAR.
teach.b: The whole people, past and future, at the foot of one mountain. Jews mark that day every year, at the festival of Shavuot.

how: Jews celebrate the giving of the Torah at Sinai on the festival of Shavuot, seven weeks after Passover; some stay up all night studying Torah, and the Ten Commandments are read aloud in synagogue.

games.q: the covenant has just been read aloud to you and the whole camp. what do you answer?
o: we will do, and we will hear.
games.why: na'aseh v'nishma: doing first. the rabbis say a heavenly voice called it the secret the angels use.

practice: Forty-five seconds, with the bell. Think of one good thing you've been putting off until you understand it better, or feel more ready. A call.
An apology. A habit. Picture yourself doing it first, and letting the understanding come afterward.

wordCard.voice: Sinai. The mountain of the covenant, where the people answered: we will do, and we will hear. Tenth word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Sinai. the name's origin is uncertain.

carryVoice: Your line: do first. The understanding tends to arrive a little later. Day ten, done.
